title: Batching-aware Rollback Advisor: cost-simulated safe apply & recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Config changes that tweak batching, KV-cache TTLs, or prefix-caching often improve overall unit cost but can transiently increase tail latency or drop SLOs for a subset of routes. Existing change-apply flows do simple preflight checks and metric gates; they don't simulate economic trade-offs nor reconcile partial state when controllers fail mid-apply. Goal: build an autonomous Rollback Advisor that (1) simulates cost/latency impact of batching and caching parameter changes using recent traffic traces, (2) attaches confidence and risk bands to each proposed config, (3) drives a staged safe-apply plan (shadow, canary, ramp) with automatic rollback triggers and guided human approvals, and (4) performs deterministic state reconciliation when partial applies, providing suggested corrective steps and one-click reverts in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest 72h of request traces and estimate per-model per-route cost delta with +/-10% accuracy compared to observed post-deploy cost
Change proposals are annotated with confidence (low/medium/high) and a recommended rollout plan (shadow/canary/fast-ramp)
Automatic rollback triggers exist for: >5% p95 latency regression, >10% error-rate increase, or cost increase beyond configured guardrails
When an apply aborts mid-rollout (controller/process crash or partial KV persistence), the system produces a deterministic reconcile plan + a single-click revert action in Console
Integration tests that simulate controller restarts demonstrate safe convergence to pre-change state within 5 minutes for common failure modes
notes: Design trade-off: accurate simulation requires recent traffic shapes; for cold routes fallbacks use conservative heuristics (assume high concurrency bursts)
We will reuse the trace-sampler and offline-batcher from the Optimize team; added transform to replay with different batching profiles
To avoid noisy autoscaling interactions, proposed rollout includes 'autoscaler hold' flag during canary windows for affected pools
Recovery plan must be idempotent: run multiple times without making additional changes to safely reconcile partial manifests

progress_updates: 2026-03-04: Miguel implemented trace ingestion module; validated sampling with 2% overhead on ingress collectors
2026-03-08: Benchmarked simulator—initial cost delta estimates within 12% of observed for steady-state batching changes; edge cases noted for bursty APIs
2026-03-11: UX sync with Console: wireframe for 'advisor suggested rollout' modal approved by PM and Design (see link)
2026-03-13: Added rollback trigger hooks into policy engine; unit tests for trigger firing on synthetic latency spike added
2026-03-14: Reconciler runbook drafted; engineering lead sign-off pending security review
incident_learnings: INC-2026-01: a previous manual rollback failed when the orchestrator left orphaned routing entries — fix: reconciler must check idempotent delete semantics for routing layer
Postmortem finding: lack of cost-simulation led to a change that reduced p50 cost but increased p99 latency for long-tail customers
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulator + confidence scoring + Console annotation (offline only)
Phase 2: Safe-apply orchestration: shadow -> canary -> ramp with autoscaler hold and explicit guardrail checks
Phase 3: Reconciler hardening: deterministic state diff, one-click revert, and CRD-level idempotency for private deployments
Phase 4: Gradual rollout across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with per-deployment tuning
qa_plan: Unit tests for simulator math & stochastic replay
Chaos tests: kill controller mid-apply and assert reconciler returns to stable state
E2E dogfood on non-customer clusters for 2 weeks with observability turned on
Load tests covering bursty and long-tail route profiles
risks: Simulator divergence for routes with very sparse telemetry (cold start) — mitigated via conservative defaults
Interactions with autoscaler could mask latency regressions — mitigated by autoscaler hold and synthetic load during canaries
Reconciler complexity increases operator surface area for Private customers; will require additional docs and on-prem validation
